```{r}
#Loading necessary library
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#Reading the Data into R --> using tidyverse

Covar          <- read_csv("GSE85307_covar-1.csv")
GeneExpression <- read_csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
GeneNames      <- read_csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")
```
The Covar file contains variables about each participant: maternal age, pregnancy outcome, Gestation, Blood Draw Date, Microarray Batch Number, BMI, Vitamin D levels, and asthma. 
The Gene Expression file contains measurements of 500 gene probes across 157 samples. Each roe represents a gene probe. Each sample column contains expression measurements with the first column being probe IDs. 
The Gene Names file connects the probe IDs to gene names. For example, a probe ID can be linked to a name such as PTX3.

```{r Cleaning-Age}
#picking out just the numeric in the age column.
Covar <- Covar %>%
  #mutate is used to change the column within the data set. 
  mutate(
    #str_remove is removing the "age_years: "
    mat_age_yrs = str_remove(mat_age_yrs, "^age_years:\\s*"),
    #as.numeric is specifying that the remaining value will be a number,not a character.
    mat_age_yrs = as.numeric(mat_age_yrs))

#making sure the cleaning created a numeric and removed the characters. 
head(Covar$mat_age_yrs)
class(Covar$mat_age_yrs)
```

```{r Cleaning All Variables}
#Continuing with remaining variables. 

#Condition
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    preg_preeclampsia = str_remove(preg_preeclampsia,"^pregnancy_condition:\\s*"),
    preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia))
#Delivery
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    delivery_gestAge_wks = str_remove(delivery_gestAge_wks, "^gestation_weeks:\\s*"),
    delivery_gestAge_wks = as.numeric(delivery_gestAge_wks))
#Sample Collection
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks = str_remove(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
      "^blood_draw_at_gestation_week:\\s*"),
    sampleCollection_gestAge_wks =
      as.numeric(sampleCollection_gestAge_wks))
#Batch MicroArray
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    batch_Microarray = str_remove(batch_Microarray,
      "^microarray_hybridization_date:\\s*"),
    batch_Microarray = as.factor(batch_Microarray))
#BMI
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    mat_BMI = str_remove(mat_BMI, "^bmi_kg/m2:\\s*"),
    mat_BMI = as.numeric(mat_BMI))
#Vitamin D
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    mat_vitD = str_remove(mat_vitD,
      "^vitamind_25\\(0h\\)_ng/ml_whole_blood_baseline:\\s*"),
    mat_vitD = as.numeric(mat_vitD))
#Asthma
Covar <- Covar %>%
  mutate(
    mat_asthma = str_remove(mat_asthma, "asthma_0=healthy_1=asthmatic:\\s*"),
    mat_asthma = as.factor(mat_asthma))
```

```{r}
#Summary of Cleaned Variables. 
head(Covar %>% select(mat_age_yrs, preg_preeclampsia, delivery_gestAge_wks, sampleCollection_gestAge_wks,
                      batch_Microarray, mat_BMI, mat_vitD, mat_asthma))
```

```{r}
#Our first column is unnamed, so we will identify it. 
GeneExpression <- GeneExpression %>%
  rename(PROBEID = 1)

#we want to extract the geoID from both csv files. 
covar_ids <- Covar$geoID
expression_ids <- names(GeneExpression)[-1]

# Count how many sample IDs match
sum(covar_ids %in% expression_ids)

# Check whether any covariate sample IDs are missing from gene expression
setdiff(covar_ids, expression_ids)

# Check how many gene-expression sample IDs match the covariate data
sum(expression_ids %in% covar_ids)
```

```{r}
#selecting a gene to observe. 
#we are looking for the PROBEID that goes along with selected gene. WIPI2
My_ProbeID <- GeneNames %>%
  filter(GENE == "WIPI2") %>%
  #pull is used to extract just the probeid from the gene we want 
  pull(PROBEID)
#Finding the gene expression data using the matched probe ID
My_Gene_Expression <- GeneExpression %>%
  filter(PROBEID %in% My_ProbeID)
```

```{r}
# Extract expression values for the selected gene
WIPI2 <- GeneExpression %>%
  filter(PROBEID %in% My_ProbeID)

# Change the data from wide format to long format
# Each row will represent one sample
WIPI2_long <- WIPI2 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -PROBEID,
    names_to = "geoID",
    values_to = "gene_expression")

# Match gene expression to participant information using geoID
PlotData <- Covar %>%
  inner_join(WIPI2_long, by = "geoID")
```

```{r}
#histogram of WIPI2 Gene Expression
ggplot(PlotData, aes(x = gene_expression)) +
geom_histogram(
      bins = 20,
      fill = "purple",
      color = "white") +
    labs(
        title = "Distribution of WIPI2 Gene Expression",
        x = "WIPI2 Gene Expression",
        y = "Number of Participants",
    caption = paste("Figure 1. Distribution of WIPI2 gene expression among",
                  "157 maternal samples.\n","Bars represent the number of",
                  "participants within each gene-expression interval.")) +
theme_classic() +
    theme(
        plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 10,
        hjust = 0))
```
The histogram shows the distribution of WIPI2 gene expression across the 157 participants. The center of the
histogram lies around the 8.1-8.2 value. The shape is relatively normally distributed with a rough bell shape,
and one distinct peak. Spread is from 7.75 to 8.53.

```{r}
#Scatterplot of maternal age and My_Gene Expression
ggplot(PlotData, aes(x = mat_age_yrs, y = gene_expression)) +
  geom_point(
    color = "purple",
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    se = TRUE,
    color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Maternal Age and WIPI2 Gene Expression",
    x = "Maternal Age (years)",
    y = "WIPI2 Gene Expression",
  caption = paste("Figure 2. Association between maternal age and WIPI2 gene expression.",
                "Each point represents one\n", "participant. The black line represents",
                "the fitted linear regression, and the gray region represents the\n",
                "95% confidence interval.")) +
  theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 10,
      hjust = 0),
      plot.caption.position = "plot")
```
The scatter plot shows the relationship between Maternal Age and WIPI2 Gene Expression. The direction of
the plot shows a positive relationship between the variables, but it is very weak. The strength of association
is weak as well as the data points are scattered around the line. The gray shaded area is the 95% confidence
interval. The scatter plot does not show a strong visual association between the Gene Expression and
Maternal Age.

```{r}
#deriving categories from a continuous variable - BMI
Covar <- Covar %>%
      mutate(
        BMI_category = cut(
        mat_BMI,
        breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 25, 30, Inf),
        labels = c(
            "Underweight",
            "Normal weight",
            "Overweight",
            "Obesity"),
        right = FALSE))
# Check the new BMI categories
Covar %>%
count(BMI_category)
```

```{r}
#adding the new column to our original data set.
PlotData <- Covar %>%
    inner_join(WIPI2_long, by = "geoID")
```

```{r}
# Boxplot of WIPI2 gene expression by pregnancy outcome and BMI category
ggplot(
    PlotData,
      aes(x = preg_preeclampsia, y = gene_expression)) +
      geom_boxplot(
        fill = "purple",
        alpha = 0.6,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
        facet_wrap(~ BMI_category) +
#geom_jitter used to represent data better by showing amount of data points. 
      geom_jitter(
        width = 0.2,
        alpha = 0.4,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
      facet_wrap(~ BMI_category) +
      labs(title = "WIPI2 Gene Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and BMI Category",
            x = "Pregnancy Outcome",
            y = "WIPI2 Gene Expression",
            caption = paste("Figure 3. WIPI2 gene expression by pregnancy outcome and maternal BMI category.", "Boxes represent\n", "the interquartile range, center lines indicate medians, and whiskers show the spread of the data.\n", "BMI categories were derived from maternal BMI.")) +
      theme_classic() +
        theme(
        plot.caption = element_text(
        size = 10,
        hjust = 0),
      plot.caption.position = "plot")
```
```{r}
#creating a data frame that holds our covariate and categoricals. 
#Convert gene expression data from wide to long format
GeneExpression_long <- GeneExpression %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -PROBEID,
    names_to = "geoID",
    values_to = "gene_expression")
#combing the three data sets
CombinedData <- GeneExpression_long %>%
  inner_join(GeneNames, by = "PROBEID") %>%

```

```{r}
My_ProbeIDs
```

```{r}
#Function Creation
Gene_Plot_Function <- function(data,
                               genes,
                               continuous_var,
                               categorical_vars) {

#Identify the probe IDs for my two newly selected genes
  My_ProbeIDs <- data %>%
    filter(GENE %in% genes) %>%
    distinct(GENE, PROBEID)

#Extract gene expression data for the two newly selected genes
  PlotData <- data %>%
    inner_join(My_ProbeIDs, by = c("GENE", "PROBEID"))

#Create an empty list to store all plots
  All_Plots <- list()

#looping the plotting instructions for each gene
  for (gene in genes) {
#Assign a color to each gene #Claude helped with figuring out how to make each gene its own color. 
    gene_color <- if (gene == "JAM2") {
      "darkorange"
    } else if (gene == "PRICKLE2") {
      "forestgreen"
    }
    #one gene at a time
    GeneData <- PlotData %>%
      filter(GENE == gene)

    #HISTOGRAM: Distribution of gene expression
    Histogram <- ggplot(GeneData, aes(x = gene_expression)) +
      geom_histogram(
        bins = 20,
        fill = gene_color,
        color = "white") +
      labs(
        title = paste("Distribution of", gene, "Gene Expression"),
        x = paste(gene, "Gene Expression"),
        y = "Number of Participants") +
      theme_classic()
    
    # SCATTERPLOT: Maternal age and gene expression
    Scatterplot <- ggplot(
      GeneData,
      aes(x = .data[[continuous_var]], y = gene_expression)) +
      geom_point(
        color = gene_color,
        alpha = 0.5,
        size = 2) +
      geom_smooth(
        method = "lm",
        se = TRUE,
        color = "black") +
      labs(
        title = paste("Maternal Age and", gene, "Gene Expression"),
        x = "Maternal Age (years)",
        y = paste(gene, "Gene Expression")) +
      theme_classic()

    # BOXPLOT: Gene expression by pregnancy outcome and BMI category
    Boxplot <- ggplot(
      GeneData,
      aes(
        x = .data[[categorical_vars[1]]],
        y = gene_expression)) +
      geom_boxplot(
        fill = gene_color,
        alpha = 0.6,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
      geom_jitter(
        width = 0.2,
        alpha = 0.4,
        na.rm = TRUE) +
      facet_wrap(vars(.data[[categorical_vars[2]]])) +
      labs(
        title = paste(
          gene,
          "Gene Expression by Pregnancy Outcome and BMI Category"),
        x = "Pregnancy Outcome",
        y = paste(gene, "Gene Expression")) +
      theme_classic()

    # Store the three plots for each gene
    All_Plots[[gene]] <- list(
      Histogram = Histogram,
      Scatterplot = Scatterplot,
      Boxplot = Boxplot)

    # Display the three plots
    print(Histogram)
    print(Scatterplot)
    print(Boxplot)}

  # Return all plots
  return(All_Plots)}
```

```{r}
JAM2_PRICKLE2_Plots <- Gene_Plot_Function(
  data = CombinedData,
  genes = c("JAM2", "PRICKLE2"),
  continuous_var = "mat_age_yrs",
  categorical_vars = c("preg_preeclampsia", "BMI_category"))
```
##Analysis:

All three histograms expressing the genes WIPI2, JAM2, and PRICKLE2 are fairly normally distributed. Each gene has a tole in keeping the placenta healthy and ensuring the fetus will receive proper nutrients for development. This makes sense that all three genes would have similar distributions. 

All three scatterplots also have similar distributions for the relationship between maternal age and the gene expression. There is a very weak positive correlation between maternal age and gene expression in each scatterplot.

The boxplots do show variations between our genes. The median for WIPI2 gene expression is fairly unchanged between each BMI category in both preeclampsia and normal pregnancies. The medians for preeclampsia in the obese category for JAM2 expression differs, as Normal pregnancies have a lower median. IN the underweight category there is an outlier, but only 5 plot points is not substantial evidence. The most prominent differences in box plots are show in the PRICKLE2 gene expression. The medians for preeclampsia and normal pregnancies are different in each BMI category. To compare all three gene boxplots, I notice that the median gene expression for WIPI2 lies around 8.2. But for JAM2 and PRICKLE2 they lie around 5.5.
